<!--
Chapter template for every new chapter of the tutorials (openspec/templates/chapter.qmd).

Copy it to <tutorial>/<chapter-slug>/index.qmd (one folder per chapter, named after it, holding the chapter and its
figures/), add it to the tutorial's list on its index.qmd and to the sidebar in _quarto.yml, then replace every
<placeholder>. The rules below come from the tutorial-content spec.

Layout (as in Fundamentals of Mathematics for Physicists):
- One "#" heading: the chapter. One "##" heading per section, each a single topic with at most six definitions.
  One "###" heading per unit: a statement with its examples and exercises, or a few closely related statements.
- Material that is not part of the line of argument, such as software for symbolic computation, goes in its own
  "###" unit at the end of the section it illustrates (e.g. "### Finite groups in SymPy"); it never interrupts
  a unit.
- The chapter ends with "## Exercises": three integrative exercises that combine several sections.

Statements (def-, thm-, prp-, lem-, cor-):
- One notion per definition. Use only terms defined earlier, or cross-reference them.
- Each sits in a statement box.
- Each is followed by one Examples box with exactly ten examples of increasing complexity, then one Exercises box
  with exactly ten exercises of increasing difficulty, each with a collapsed solution. Ten, not more.
- Every solution has two tabs: "Proof" (the theoretical solution) and "SageMath" (code in a {.python .sage} block
  and its real output in a {.text .sage-output} block). For an exercise that asks for a proof, the SageMath tab
  checks the claim on a named concrete case and says it is a check, not a proof. Record the outputs with
  `python3 _filters/check_content.py <tutorial> <chapter> --update` and review the diff.
- Figures: each is drawn by a SageMath script figures/<name>.sage that starts with
  load("../../_filters/figstyle.sage") and saves with save_figure / save_threejs / save_plotly. A caption says in
  at most two sentences what the figure shows; it never names a script, a file, SageMath or another tool.
- Examples include a figure where the object can be drawn, and an interactive version for a surface or a
  vector field.

Prose:
- Every block is introduced by at least two sentences (twenty words or more) of running text. Two blocks never
  follow each other directly (a solution belongs to its exercise).
- Reading only the prose still tells what each block defines, illustrates or asks, and why it comes there.
- The chapter introduction motivates the topic on its own terms and names the sources.

Notation: follow the tutorial's notation page (<tutorial>/notation/index.qmd; for Kaluza-Klein, conventions/index.qmd),
built from the shared tables in _notation/, whatever notation the sources use. Convert formulas taken from a source,
signs and normalisations included; mention a source's convention only as a comparison that names it. Before using a
symbol that is not in the tables, add it to the right _notation/ partial (or to the notation page's "Conventions
specific to this tutorial"), reusing an existing symbol for the same object and never giving a symbol a second meaning.

Sources: use the textbooks the reading notes (Zotero child notes tagged tutorial-reading-note) map to this chapter.
Rewrite in your own voice, in the site notation, and cite at the point of use with section and problem numbers ([@key, Sec. n], [@key, Problem n]).
Every cited key exists in references/references.bib.

Identifiers are number-free slugs (sec-, def-, thm-, exm-, exr-, fig-, eq-), unique across the tutorial. The
exm-/exr- suffixes -01 ... -10 below are placeholders: give each block a descriptive slug.
-->
